newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank says Dutch central bank may hike again.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank says Dutch central bank may hike again.

text.p: Rabobank International said on Monday the Dutch central bank may lift interest rates again if the guilder continued to weaken against the German mark.
It said the mark failed to fall below 1.1240 guilders after the central bank raised the special advances rate to 2.70 percent from 2.50 percent last Thursday.

If the rate was to break up through 1.1256, the central parity rate in the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) of 1.1267 would beckon. "The Dutch central bank will leave no doubts as to where its priority rests ... a strong guilder," Rabobank International said in its Financial Weekly report.
It said a rise in the mark above 1.1256 guilders was likely to trigger another unilateral hike in the special advances rate of 10 to 20 basis points.
The mark was trading at 1.1247 at 1455 GMT.
The special advances rate is the Dutch equivalent of Germany's repo rate, which is currently 3.00 percent.
Rabobank said a rate hike would almost certaintly mean the central bank would raise its equivalent of Germany's discount rate, the secured loans rate, which is now 2.00 percent.
The German discount rate is 2.50 percent.

"Although the central bank would point to the technical character of such a hike as well, it could lead to market speculation that this would signal the end of the rate cycle in Continental Europe, given the twin-brother relationship of the Dutch central bank and the Bundesbank," Rabobank said.
But the impressive Dutch current account surplus, against a deficit in Germany, implied a strengthening in the guilder.

The bank said the possibility of a Dutch rate hike, the fact that all continental European ERM currencies had lost ground to the mark and the structurally better shape of the Dutch economy also argued for a reversal of the guilder downtrend.
